chunks: So al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Abi Sa'id, who said:

I said to Abi Ibrahim عليه السلام: May a man apply dye while he is junub? He said: "No." I said: Then may he become junub while he is dyed? He said: "No." Then he was silent for a little while, then he said: "O Aba Sa'id, shall I not direct you to something that you may do?" I said: Yes. He said: "When you apply henna, and the henna has taken its proper effect and fully settled, then at that time have intercourse."

key_terms.جُنُبٌ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.مَأْخَذَهُ: its proper hold or effect on the body
key_terms.مُخْتَضِبٌ: being in a state of having dye applied or wearing dye

ai.seo_question: Can a person apply henna while in janabah or become junub while dyed according to Imam Abi Ibrahim عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses a ruling related to applying henna and the state of janabah. Imam Abi Ibrahim عليه السلام initially forbids both applying dye while junub and entering janabah while one is in the process of being dyed, then instructs that intercourse should take place after the henna has fully taken effect.
